q: 501. Different types of pitched roofs are ...........
explain: Pitched roofs are categorized by their shape and slope; Gable roofs have two sloping sides meeting at a ridge, while Mansard roofs have four sides with two different slopes on each side.

q: 502. The roof having slope in all four directions is called ...........
explain: A hip roof (or hipped roof) has slopes on all four sides which meet at the corners to form 'hips'.

q: 503. Apex line of a sloping roof is called ...........
explain: The ridge is the horizontal peak where two opposing sloping surfaces meet at the top of the roof.

q: 504. Lower edge of the inclined roof surface is called ...........
explain: Eaves (or eves) are the edges of the roof which overhang the face of the wall and normally carry the guttering.

q: 505. The shell roof may be designed as ...........
options: both thin shell and thick shell
explain: Shell structures can be classified based on their thickness-to-radius ratio; thin shells rely on membrane action, while thick shells consider transverse shear.

q: 506. The standard length of Asbestos cement corrugated sheet should be ...........
explain: A.C. corrugated sheets are manufactured in standard lengths of 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, and 3.0 meters (or equivalent imperial measurements) to suit different purlin spacings.

q: 507. A truss having upper and lower pitch, and made by combining king and queen post trusses, also used as a roof, is known as ...........
explain: A Mansard truss provides two different slopes on the same side, often utilized to create habitable attic space.

q: 508. The roof, suitable for large assembly hall, will be a ...........
explain: Shell roofs are ideal for large assembly halls because they can cover vast spans without the need for internal pillars or columns.

q: 509. The shell roof preferred for industrial roofing is ...........
explain: North light shell roofs are used in factories to provide uniform, glare-free natural light by facing the glazed portions toward the north.

q: 510. The short piece of timber bolted to the rafters of a roof truss fixing the purlin in position are named as ...........
explain: Cleats are small blocks of wood or steel angles fixed to the principal rafters to prevent the purlins from sliding down.

q: 511. The maximum size of aggregate used in D.P.C. is about ...........
explain: For a Damp Proof Course (DPC), which is usually only 2.5cm to 4cm thick, the aggregate size is limited to 10mm to ensure proper compaction and impermeability.

q: 512. The inclined braces used in a truss to prevent the sagging of the principal rafters are called as ...........
explain: Struts are compression members in a truss that support the principal rafters and prevent them from bending under the load of the purlins.

q: 513. In the king post truss the member used to prevent the sagging of beam and connected with the ridge is called ...........
explain: The King Post is the central vertical tension member that 'hangs' from the ridge to support the center of the tie beam.

q: 514. In village houses the material used for covering the pitched roof is ...........
explain: Thatch (dried straw, reeds, or grass) is a traditional, locally available roofing material common in rural or village settings.

q: 515. C.G.I. roof covering stands for ...........
explain: CGI sheets are steel sheets that have been galvanized with zinc for corrosion resistance and corrugated for structural stiffness.

q: 516. In asbestos cement corrugated sheet roofing, the minimum horizontal lap in meters should be ...........
explain: A minimum end (horizontal) lap of 150mm (0.15m) is required to prevent water from entering through the joints during heavy rain.

q: 517. Generally while plastering in ordinary buildings, the ratio of cement and sand used in cement plaster should be ...........
explain: A 1:6 ratio (1 part cement to 6 parts sand) is standard for internal plastering on brick or stone walls.

q: 518. The roughening of solid background to provide suitable key for plastering is called ...........
explain: Hacking is the process of making small grooves or indents in a smooth surface (like concrete) so the plaster can bond effectively.

q: 519. Dislodgement of plaster work from the background is known as ...........
explain: Peeling occurs when the bond between the plaster and the wall fails, causing the plaster to fall off in layers.

q: 520. The surface to which the first coat of plaster is applied is called ...........
explain: The background surface is the bare masonry or concrete wall that receives the initial layer of plaster.

q: 521. The development of one or more local swelling on the finished plastered surface, is called ...........
explain: Blistering is a defect caused by the presence of unslaked lime or trapped air/moisture behind the plaster coat.

q: 522. Which of the following pointing is extensively used in brick work and stone masonry face work?
explain: Flush pointing is the most common because it is simple, durable, and does not provide a ledge for dust or water to collect.

q: 523. A rolling shutter is often used for ...........
explain: Rolling shutters provide high security and occupy minimal space, making them the standard choice for storefronts (shops) and garages.

q: 524. In king post the number of vertical posts is ...........
explain: A King Post truss is characterized by exactly one central vertical post.

q: 525. For pointing the masonry is raked out to a depth of about ...........
explain: To ensure a strong bond for the new mortar, joints should be raked to a depth of 15-20 mm before pointing.

q: 526. The development of a series of hair cracks on the finished surface, plastered usually in haphazard manner, is called ...........
explain: Crazing refers to fine network of cracks caused by shrinkage of the cement during drying, often due to excessive cement or rich mix.

q: 527. In a three coat plastering, the third coat known as ...........
explain: In three-coat work, the coats are: 1. Rendering coat, 2. Floating coat, and 3. Setting (or finishing) coat.

q: 528. Screws for wood work as specified by ...........
explain: Wood screws are commercially classified by their length and their 'gauge' (diameter of the shank).

q: 529. In which of the following arch, the center the arch is above the springing line?
explain: A Horse-shoe arch (Moorish arch) has a curve that continues beyond the semi-circle, putting the center above the springing line.

q: 530. Which of the following scaffolding is provided for a building on the side of a busy street where the ordinary scaffolding will obstruct the traffic on road?
explain: Needle scaffolding (or cantilever scaffolding) is supported by 'needles' projecting through the wall, leaving the ground clear for traffic.

q: 531. A temporary rigid structure having platforms to enable masons to work at different stages of a building is known as ...........
explain: Scaffolding is the temporary framework used to support workers and materials during construction or repair.

q: 532. The arrangement of supporting an existing structure by providing supports underneath, is known as ...........
explain: Underpinning is the process of strengthening or deepening the foundation of an existing building or structure.

q: 533. Type of pointing in which V shaped projection is provided outside the wall surface is called ...........
explain: Toothed (or weathered) pointing involves creating a sloped or V-projection to help shed water from the joints.

q: 534. Brick floors are used in ...........
explain: While used in many places, brick flooring is highly characteristic of railway platforms due to its durability and grip.

q: 535. In multistoried government buildings, the floor height is usually restricted to ...........
explain: A clear height of 3.4 meters is common in public/government buildings to allow for better ventilation and larger room sizes.

q: 536. The thickness of square or rectangular stones used in flagstone flooring varies from ...........
explain: Flagstones are usually 30mm to 50mm thick, providing a heavy-duty wearing surface.

q: 537. While laying cement concrete floor, the floor is divided into small panels. The length of the panel is restricted to ...........
explain: To prevent shrinkage cracks in large areas, concrete floors are laid in panels usually not exceeding 2 meters in length.

q: 538. Keeping in view possibility of shrinkage and wrapping the width of the boards is recommended to be ...........
explain: Narrower boards (approx. 10 cm) are less prone to significant warping or 'cupping' compared to wider boards.

q: 539. Broken bricks or stone chips are also called ...........
explain: Spalls are small chips or fragments of stone or brick, often used as filling material.

q: 540. In residential buildings the height of bathroom should not be less than ...........
explain: Under building bylaws, bathrooms usually have a minimum height requirement of 2.4 meters.

q: 541. The weight of river sand per cubic meter, is taken as ...........
explain: The density of typical river sand ranges from 1800 to 1900 kg/m³ depending on moisture content.

q: 542. For walls built in cement mortar 1:6, the minimum thickness for single storied building is ...........
explain: A standard 20 cm (9 inch) wall is the minimum requirement for load-bearing brickwork in a single-story building.

q: 543. The lime sand mortar normally used in brick construction has a ratio of ...........
explain: Lime mortar traditionally uses a richer 1:2 ratio (1 part lime to 2 parts sand) compared to cement mortars.

q: 544. The ratio of cement-sand mortar preferred in load bearing walls is ...........
explain: 1:6 cement mortar offers a good balance of strength and economy for load-bearing masonry.

q: 545. The nominal thickness of one-brick (un-plastered) wall is about ...........
explain: One-brick wall thickness is approximately 200 mm (including the mortar joint).

q: 546. The portion of wall on which the end of an arch rests is known as ...........
explain: The abutment is the masonry mass that supports the ends of an arch and resists its lateral thrust.

q: 547. The type of arch used for high class buildings where appearance is of prime importance, is known as ...........
explain: Gauged arches use bricks precisely cut to size and shape, allowing for very fine joints and a decorative look.

q: 548. A temporary structure to support an arch during construction is called ...........
explain: Centering is the temporary timber or steel framework that holds the bricks/stones of an arch in place until the mortar sets.

q: 549. A pointed arch which forms equilateral or isosceles triangle is known as ...........
explain: A lancet arch is a narrow, sharply pointed arch characteristic of Gothic architecture.

q: 550. In jack arch floor, the rise given to the arch is ...........
explain: Jack arches are very shallow; the rise is typically kept to 1/12th of the span to minimize the vertical profile.

q: 551. Springers are those wedge shaped blocks of an arch which are provided at
explain: Springers are the first wedge-shaped units (voussoirs) placed at the ends of an arch, resting directly on the impost or the support (skewback) at the extremes.

q: 552. The perpendicular distance between intrados and extrados of an arch is called
explain: The depth of an arch is defined as the perpendicular distance between its inner curve (intrados) and its outer curve (extrados).

q: 553. The bulk density of aggregates is generally expressed as
explain: In standard construction practice and SI units, the bulk density of aggregates (mass per unit volume) is typically expressed in kg/m³.

q: 554. The type of aggregates of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted are
explain: Rounded spherical aggregates have the least surface area for a given volume and, when compacted, leave the minimum amount of voids compared to angular or flaky shapes.

q: 555. If the average compressive strength is 4000 kg/cm² and standard deviation is 500, the coefficient of variation is
explain: The coefficient of variation is calculated as (Standard Deviation / Mean) × 100. Here, (500 / 4000) × 100 = 12.5%.

q: 556. Addition of pozzolana to ordinary Portland cement causes
explain: While pozzolana reduces the initial rate of strength gain, it reacts with calcium hydroxide to produce additional C-S-H gel, leading to higher ultimate strength and better durability.

q: 557. Setting time of cement increases by adding
explain: Gypsum (calcium sulphate dihydrate) acts as a retarder in cement, preventing flash set and increasing the time available for mixing and placing.

q: 558. Setting time of cement decreases by adding
explain: Calcium chloride acts as an accelerator, speeding up the hydration process and significantly reducing the setting time of the concrete.

q: 559. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking is the increase in the volume of dry sand caused by the formation of a thin film of water around the sand particles, which creates surface tension and pushes the grains apart.

q: 560. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
explain: Limestone (calcareous material) provides the calcium oxide (CaO) which is the primary constituent (about 60-67%) required for cement production.

q: 561. Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured from
explain: OPC is primarily made from calcareous materials (limestone) and argillaceous materials (clay), which provide the necessary calcium, silica, and alumina.

q: 562. Workability of concrete is measured by
explain: The slump test is the most common field test used to measure the consistency and workability of fresh concrete.

q: 563. Specified compressive strength of concrete is obtained from cube tests at the end of
explain: Concrete is traditionally assumed to reach its full characteristic design strength at 28 days of proper curing.

q: 564. Allowable shear strength of concrete depends on
explain: In design codes like IS 456, the permissible shear strength (τc) is a function of the grade of concrete (compressive strength) and the percentage of steel.

q: 565. Le Chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
explain: This apparatus measures the expansion of cement due to free lime, which indicates the 'soundness' or volume stability of the material.

q: 566. Slump test is done for
explain: The slump test is specifically designed to determine the workability and fluidity of a fresh concrete mix.

q: 567. Particles of 0.002 mm size are that of
explain: According to the Unified Soil Classification System (USCS), particles smaller than 0.002 mm (2 microns) are classified as clay.

q: 568. Gypsum is added for
explain: Gypsum is a retarder added during the grinding of clinker to prevent flash setting by slowing down the hydration of C3A.

q: 569. The mixture of different ingredients of cement is burnt at
explain: In a rotary kiln, the raw materials reach a temperature of approximately 1400°C to 1500°C to form clinker through chemical fusion.

q: 570. The cement whose strength is a little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength is known as
explain: Low heat cement reduces the rate of chemical heat evolution, resulting in slower early strength development but achieving full strength over time.

q: 571. For construction of structures in sea water, the cement generally preferred to is
explain: PPC is preferred in marine environments because it offers higher resistance to chemical attacks (sulfates and chlorides) and has lower permeability.

q: 572. The initial and final setting time for O.P.C. are approximately related as
explain: This is an empirical relationship where 't' is the initial setting time in minutes. For standard OPC (30m initial), T = 530 + 30 = 560m (~10 hours).

q: 573. The diameter of needle in vicats apparatus for the determination of initial setting time is prescribed as
explain: A 1 mm square or circular needle is used to penetrate the cement paste for measuring the initial setting time.

q: 574. If the angularity number of aggregate is increased, then the workability of the concrete using this aggregate will
explain: A higher angularity number indicates more angular particles, which create more internal friction and require more water/paste, thus decreasing workability.

q: 575. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
explain: Fineness Modulus (FM) is an index of the average particle size; a higher value means the aggregate is coarser.

q: 576. I.S.I. has specified the full strength of concrete after
explain: The standard characteristic strength of concrete is officially determined by testing cubes after a 28-day curing period.

q: 577. The shuttering of hall measuring 4 m × 5 m can be removed after
explain: For spans up to 4.5m, the soffit formwork to slabs can typically be removed after 7 days as per Indian Standards.

q: 578. For compacting plain concrete road surface of thickness less than 20 cm, we use
explain: Screed vibrators (or surface vibrators) are ideal for thin slabs and road surfaces to ensure compaction and a level finish simultaneously.

q: 579. The final operation of finishing floors, is known as
explain: Troweling is the final stage of finishing where a steel trowel is used to create a smooth, dense, and wear-resistant surface.

q: 580. The operation of removing humps and hollows of uniform concrete surface is known as
explain: Screeding is the process of striking off excess concrete to bring the top surface to the proper grade and remove irregularities.

q: 581. The type of aggregates not suitable for high strength concrete and for pavements subjected to tension is
explain: Rounded aggregates have poor interlocking properties compared to angular aggregates, making them less suitable for high-strength or tension-prone structures.

q: 582. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if the aggregates are
explain: Rounded aggregates have the minimum surface area and least internal friction, which allows the mix to flow more easily for a given water content.

q: 583. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
explain: While standard definitions vary by code (often 1.8x), in this specific textbook context, an aggregate is considered elongated if its length is significantly greater (often taken as 2x) than its mean dimension.

q: 584. On grading curve, the gap grading is represented by
explain: A horizontal line on a grain size distribution curve indicates that a range of particle sizes is missing, which defines gap grading.

q: 585. Initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement is
explain: As per IS codes, the initial setting time for OPC should not be less than 30 minutes.

q: 586. The maximum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: Coarse aggregates are generally defined as particles that are retained on a 4.75 mm sieve, with a maximum size typically reaching 75 mm to 80 mm.

q: 587. The sum of percentage of all deleterious materials in the aggregate shall not exceed
explain: To ensure concrete durability, the total amount of deleterious substances (clay, silt, organic matter) should be limited to 5% by weight.

q: 588. The resistance of an aggregate to compressive force is known as
explain: The Aggregate Crushing Value (ACV) provides a relative measure of resistance to crushing under a gradually applied compressive load.

q: 589. The resistance of an aggregate to the effect of hydration of cement and weather is called
explain: Aggregate soundness refers to its ability to resist volume changes due to environmental factors like freezing/thawing or salt crystallization.

q: 590. The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as
explain: Abrasion value measures the hardness and resistance of aggregates to surface wear and attrition (rubbing).

q: 591. Bulking of sand is
options: increase in volume of sand due to presence of moisture upto certain extent
explain: Bulking is the physical expansion of sand volume when moisture forms a film around grains, reaching a peak at about 4-6% moisture content.

q: 592. In order to obtain the best workability of concrete, the preferred shape of aggregate is
explain: Rounded aggregates facilitate easier movement of particles within the mix due to reduced friction, improving flowability.

q: 593. Bulking of sand is maximum if moisture content is about
explain: Maximum bulking typically occurs when the moisture content is in the range of 4% to 5%.

q: 594. Finer grinding of cement
options: affects only the early development of strength
explain: Finer cement has more surface area for hydration, which speeds up early strength gain but does not significantly change the ultimate strength reached at long ages.

q: 595. Poisons ratio for concrete
explain: Poisson's ratio for concrete typically ranges between 0.15 to 0.20 and generally increases slightly with richer (stronger) mixes.

q: 596. 1% of voids in concrete mix would reduce its strength by about
explain: Voids significantly impact density; a general rule of thumb in concrete technology is that every 1% of air voids can reduce compressive strength by roughly 5% to 6%.

q: 597. The fineness modulus of fine aggregate is in the range of
explain: Fine aggregate (sand) typically has a Fineness Modulus between 2.0 and 3.5 (Fine: 2.2-2.6, Medium: 2.6-2.9, Coarse: 2.9-3.2).

q: 598. Minimum grade of concrete to be used in R.C.C. as per I.S. 456: 2000 is
explain: IS 456:2000 specifies that for reinforced concrete work, a grade lower than M20 should not be used (M15 was the limit in the 1978 version).

q: 599. Minimum quantity of water needed per 50 kg of cement for M15 grade of concrete is
explain: Standard water-cement ratios for M15 often fall around 0.6, which roughly equates to 30-32 liters per 50 kg bag.

q: 600. In case of hand mixing of concrete, the extra cement to be added is
explain: Hand mixing is less efficient than machine mixing, so 10% extra cement is usually added to compensate for potential inconsistencies.
